title.narrative: Integrated nutrition and health support to address malnutrition-Tigray Region North West and Central Zone(Seven Woredas)

description.narrative: ltpgtMultiple interwoven humanitarian crises, such as protracted latent conflicts and climatic disturbances—including extended droughts and inundations—have significantly exacerbated humanitarian needs. ltbrgtAccording to the 2025 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO), over 19 million people require humanitarian assistance, including more than 1 million refugees hosted in the country.nbspClimate-related adversities, encompassing droughts and floods, continue to jeopardize the livelihoods of vulnerable populations and impede access to fundamental necessities and services across various zones of the country. This project endeavors to support droughtnbsp-affected communities with limited access to essential services provided by humanitarian partners and governmental structures, thereby mitigating morbidity and mortality in Asgede, Laelay Koraro, Shire Endaslasie town, Tahtay Adiyabo IDP sites, as well as Zana and Tahtay Adiyabo Woredas in the North West Zone, and Adet Woreda in the Central Zone of the Tigray region. The Health and Nutrition sector's response, with the integration of protection activities in accordance with the reserve allocation of the Emergency Health Fund (EHF), encompasses the health and nutrition efforts in the targeted Woredas. The intervention will address health exigencies by concentrating on the provision of essential primary healthcare services through Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNTs) while fortifying systems, including maternal and child health initiatives. It will also enhance routine and emergency immunization efforts, bolster surveillance activities, and facilitate the prevention and management of communicable diseases. Additionally, the project will focus on capacity building for government healthcare providers, risk communication, and community engagement, as well as ensuring the operational functionality of health facilities through the provision of medicines, medical supplies, and minor repairs and furnishings of health facilities. The Nutrition component aspires to deliver life-saving nutritional interventions by integrating Community-based Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) and Infant and Young Child Feeding in Emergencies (IYCF-E) activities through the existing health infrastructure. The mainstreaming of protection across the sector will encompass risk mitigation, the provision of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) referral and support services, and the strengthening of essential services, including psychosocial support initiatives.nbspltbrgtThe SMART Survey Plus conducted b/n July 4 and August 8,2024 showed that 32.93% (95% CI:30.9-35.0) of sampled households had an acceptable food consumption score, while 36.6% (95%CI: 29.6-44.2) had a poor score. Additionally, 1% (95%CI:0.4-2.6) of households experienced severe hunger, and 41.4% (95% CI:33.1-50.2) faced moderate hunger. Many households are resorting to negative coping strategies, such as limiting portion sizes and reducing the number of meals eaten daily. The survey also indicated that deworming coverage for children aged 12 to 59 months was recorded at 46.1%.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe project is designed to deliver a comprehensive, vulnerability-centric, and needs-driven multi-sectoral response for individuals facing pressing challenges in Tigray. It aspires to fortify health and nutrition services specifically within the seven woredas by synergizing emergency health and nutrition initiatives, the endeavor aims to ameliorate nutritional conditions among at-risk communities with a primary emphasis on enhancing overall health and wellbeing. A total of 1,000,000.00 USD proposed for the intended health and Nutrition activities for 6nbspmonths project period. In the life of the project a total of 88,613 (Women 25,309, Girls 19,887, Men 24,317 and Boys 19,100)) targeted in seven woredas.ltbrgtlt/pgt
